title: Compare regions with a flame graph

blocks.content:
With the slow region isolated, compare it against a healthy one to pinpoint the exact function responsible.

To compare with flame graphs, complete the following steps:

blocks.reftarget: section[data-testid='data-testid Panel header eu-west-1'] button[aria-label='Flame graph']
blocks.content: Select the **Flame graph** for the `eu-west-1` process.

The flame graph is a top-down view of the total time the process spends in each function. This process receives gRPC requests, so the stack starts by handling incoming gRPC requests and then descends down the call stack. How to read it: each node is a function, and its **width** is the share of CPU time spent in that function plus everything it calls, so wider nodes cost more. A function's callees are stacked directly beneath it. **Self** time is spent in the function itself; **total** time is the function plus its callees. For more, see Flame graphs and self vs. total metrics. Looking at this flame graph, a lot of time is spent in functions related to regex. To understand why `eu-west-1` is slower than the other regions, go back and compare.
Return to the grouped **region** view for `checkoutservice`, the same view you left off on.

Now compare the slow process to a healthy one. `eu-west-1` is significantly more expensive than the others, so you'll set a healthy region (`ap-south-1`) as the baseline and `eu-west-1` as the comparison.
Click **Compare** to open the diff flame graph for the two regions.
To compare the same time window in both, highlight a spike in the **Comparison** graph and click **Sync time ranges**, or click **Auto-select** to line up the time windows automatically.
The diff flame graph appears. Similar to a git diff, red highlights what was added in the comparison (`eu-west-1`) and green highlights what was removed relative to the baseline (`ap-south-1`).
To focus on your own code rather than library logic, type `main` into the table's search bar.

You can see that `PlaceOrder` calls `processOrder`, which calls `validateOrderWithRegex`. Hovering over each function shows that `eu-west-1` spends a huge amount of time in `validateOrderWithRegex`, unlike `ap-south-1`, so this confirms that this is the cause of our increased CPU usage.
You've found the function responsible for the regional slowdown. Next is an optional AI look at a flame graph.
